fact: Ashton Estates' architectural standards require a detailed landscaping plan for any lot to be approved by the Architectural Review Committee before the landscaping is installed.
quote: All proposed landscaping to occur on any lot shall be submitted in a detailed landscaping plan for approval by the Architectural Review Committee prior to the landscaping being installed.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 17
notes: Neither these standards nor the declaration mentions artificial turf, synthetic turf or putting greens (standards read in full from the PDF text layer; the 35-page declaration scan OCR'd and the cited pages checked against the page images, 2026-09-26).

fact: In Ashton Estates, landscaping and other changes made after a home is finished must go to the Architectural Review Committee for approval before they begin.
quote: Additional construction to a home, landscaping or other improvements to a home after completion of an approved home must be submitted to the Architectural Review Committee for approval prior to initiating such changes and/or additions.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 2 (Additional Construction and/or Exterior Changes after Completion of Original Construction)

fact: The Ashton Estates declaration counts landscaping, removing grass or plants, and grading, excavation or any change of grade or drainage pattern as an Improvement to Property that needs the committee's approval.
quote: "Improvement to Property," requiring approval of the Association Architectural Review Committee, shall mean and include, without limitation: … (c) the grading, excavation, filling or similar disturbance to the surface of the land including, without limitation, change of grade, change of ground level, change of drainage pattern or change of stream bed; (d) landscaping, planting, clearing or removing of trees, shrubs, grass or plants
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article IX, Section 4
notes: Read on the page image (recorded page 24 of 35).

fact: At Ashton Estates' 2023 annual meeting the manager said the community would need three pre-approved xeriscaping plans under new state requirements, and when an owner asked whether artificial turf would be allowed in them, no answer was given.
quote: … the community will be required to have 3 pre-approved xeriscaping plans available to residents as part of new state requirements. A question was asked if artificial turf will be allowed in the plans. No answer was given.
source_label: Ashton Estates Community Association 2023 Annual Meeting minutes, September 28, 2023 (in the 2024 Annual Meeting Packet)
notes: Speaker's name elided. The minutes were circulated with the September 2024 annual-meeting packet. No later posted record (2025 minutes, 2025 newsletters, policies page) answers the turf question.

fact: The Ashton Estates declaration submits the subdivision to the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act.
quote: Additionally, Declarant hereby submits the real estate identified above to the provisions of the Colorado Common Interest Ownership Act Sections 38-33.3-101 (the Act), et. seq., Colorado Revised Statutes, as it may be amended from time to time.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Preamble
notes: The 2024 annual-meeting notice also calls the association 'a Common Interest Community'. Read on the page image (recorded page 6 of 35).

fact: Ashton Estates' declaration allows each home to be used only as a single-family residence.
quote: No Living Unit shall be used for any other purpose other than as a single-family residence, and no business or commercial activity shall be carried on or within the Project other than those home occupations defined as such in the City of Greeley Zoning Code.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article VI, Section 3
notes: Detached houses on lots of about two acres (see lot-acreage); read on the page image (recorded page 17 of 35).

fact: The Ashton Estates declaration covers 43 lots in three blocks of a residential subdivision of the City of Greeley in Weld County.
quote: Lots 1 - 27 of Block 1, Lots 1 - 8 of Block 2 and Lots 1 - 8 of Block 3 of Ashton Estates, a residential subdivision of the City of Greeley, Weld County, Colorado.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Preamble
notes: 43 = 27 + 8 + 8. The association's 2025 budget also bills '$310/Lot for 43 lots' (2024 Annual Meeting Packet).

fact: Ashton Estates' association gives its location as 65th Avenue and Ashcroft Road in Greeley and describes the neighborhood as homes on large acreages.
quote: Homes on large acreages … covenant protected estate lots … 65th Avenue and Ashcroft Road, Greeley, Colorado 80634, United States

fact: Ashton Estates' standards keep buildings at least 35 feet from the front and rear lot lines and 30 feet from each side lot line.
quote: No building shall be located on any site nearer than 35 feet to the front of the lot nor 35 feet to the rear of the lot lines. No building shall be located nearer than 30 feet to any side lot line.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 12

fact: Ashton Estates' declaration allows horses on any lot, no more than two per lot or one per acre.
quote: Horses may be kept within any Lot within the Project subject to the limitation that the number of horses shall not exceed two (2) horses per Lot regardless of the size of the Lot or one (1) horse per acre.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article VI, Section 12
notes: Read on the page image (recorded page 18 of 35); horse fencing and any barn or feed storage go through architectural approval.

fact: Ashton Estates' standards encourage grade-level decks, patios and outside living areas, discourage large elevated decks or patios, and send site grading to the committee for approval.
quote: Grade level decks, patios and outside living areas are encouraged and large elevated decks or patios are discouraged. Site grading shall be submitted to and approved by the Architectural Review Committee.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 16 (Site Grading)

fact: An Ashton Estates landscaping plan may not alter any drainage, wetland or utility easement shown on the subdivision's recorded plat.
quote: Any landscaping plan must also recognize the existence of and not alter in any manner any drainage, wetland or utility easement shown on the recorded Plat for Ashton Estates as those easements affect any lot within the subdivision.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 17

fact: In Ashton Estates, an exterior light source should not be visible from neighboring homes, and the committee approves where every exterior light goes.
quote: The light source should not be visible from adjoining dwellings, and the location of all exterior lighting shall be approved by the Architectural Review Committee.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 19

fact: Ashton Estates prefers open white PVC two- or three-rail fencing and limits the outside edge of perimeter lots to three-rail white vinyl ranch fence 50 inches high.
quote: The preferred fencing throughout the subdivision shall be a white plastic PVC two- or three-rail open fencing pattern. Perimeter fencing on the exterior side on any outside lot shall be restricted to three-rail, white vinyl PVC ranch style, 50” in height with post 8’ on center (after 10/21/04).
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 14
notes: The PDF's text layer prints the inch and foot marks as '@' and '='; they are restored here. Amended by the Ashton Estates Executive Board 10/21/04.

fact: Ashton Estates bans wire and chain-link fences, except an animal run the committee approves that is also screened, and screening for a dog run must use materials similar to the house's siding.
quote: Screening fences for trash receptacles, dog runs or other similar purposes shall require use of screening materials which are similar to exterior siding materials of the residence or other accessory buildings built upon a lot. No fence shall be constructed on any lot which is made of wire or chain link materials. The Architectural Review Committee may approve an animal run which is built of wire or chain link materials provided any such fencing is also screened with materials acceptable to the Architectural Review Committee.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 14

fact: Ashton Estates requires committee approval before building ancillary improvements to existing homes, a list that includes dog runs, fencing, exterior lights and play equipment.
quote: All proposed ancillary improvements to existing homes in the Ashton Estates Subdivision must be submitted to the Architectural Review Committee for approval prior to commencement of construction. Such improvements include, but are not limited to: additions, decks, exterior light, dog runs, fencing, basketball hoops, play equipment, antenna, satellite dishes, re-staining/painting of the home or fencing in a new color and solar collectors.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 6

fact: Ashton Estates' Architectural Review Committee commits to a written response within 14 working days after a complete submittal.
quote: Upon receipt of all required documents, the Architectural Review Committee will review the plans and will provide a written response to the Owner and/or Builder within fourteen (14) working days after submittal.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 4
notes: Sec. 6 gives the same 14 working days for ancillary improvements to existing homes.

fact: Under the Ashton Estates declaration, a request is deemed approved if the committee sends no disapproval or request for more information within 30 days of receiving all required materials.
quote: Any request for approval of a proposed Improvement to Property shall be deemed approved, unless disapproval or a request for additional information or materials is transmitted to the Applicant by the Association Architectural Review Committee within thirty (30) days after the date of receipt by the Association Architectural Review Committee of all required materials
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article IX, Section 12
notes: Read on the page image (recorded page 25 of 35). Section 10 separately requires a written decision within 30 days of all materials, with reasons stated for a denial.

fact: Ashton Estates' ARC application page lists landscaping among the property improvements it reviews and tells owners the committee will respond within 14 working days and that a project is automatically approved if the ARC has not answered after 30 days.
quote: Examples of Property Improvements Buildings, fencing, dog runs, shops, barn, change house color, additions, landscaping, decks, swimming pools, and sheds/storage structures. … 4. The committee will respond to you within 14 working days. 5. If you do not hear from the ARC after 30 days, your project is automatically approved.
source_label: Ashton Estates Homeowners Association website, ARC Application page

fact: The Ashton Estates improvement application asks for plans with location, elevations and dimensions, specifications such as a manufacturer's brochure, color and material samples and photographs, and the owner agrees to start no work before written approval.
quote: Plans including location elevations, and dimensions Specifications (e.g., manufacturer’s brochure) Samples of colors Samples of description of materials Photographs … 1. No work or commitment of work will be made by me until I have received written approval from the Association.
source_label: Ashton Estates Application for Approval of Architectural Improvements (fillable PDF)

fact: The Ashton Estates improvement application commits the owner to tell the committee in writing when approved work is done so it can be inspected against the approval.
quote: 10. In the event of approval, I will notify the Architectural Control Committee in writing when the work is completed so that an inspection can be made to ensure that it conforms to what was approved.
source_label: Ashton Estates Application for Approval of Architectural Improvements (fillable PDF), item 10

fact: Under the Ashton Estates declaration, finished work is deemed to comply if the committee gives no notice of noncompliance within 30 days after receiving the owner's written Notice of Completion.
quote: If, for any reason other than the Applicant's act or neglect, the Association Architectural Review Committee fails to notify the Applicant of any noncompliance within thirty (30) days after receipt by the Association Architectural Review Committee of written Notice of Completion from the Applicant, the Improvement to Property shall be deemed in compliance if the Improvement to Property was, in fact, completed as of the date of the Notice of Completion.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article IX, Section 18
notes: Section 16 gives the committee the right to inspect before, during or after completion. Read on the page images (recorded pages 26-27 of 35).

fact: An Ashton Estates owner can appeal a committee denial or condition to the association's Executive Board by written notice within 20 days.
quote: If the Association Architectural Review Committee denies, imposes conditions on, or refuses approval of a proposed Improvement to Property, the Applicant may appeal to the Executive Board of the Association by giving written notice of such appeal to the Association Architectural Review Committee within twenty (20) days after such denial or refusal.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article IX, Section 11

fact: An Ashton Estates approval is valid for 12 months; if construction has not begun by then, the plans must be resubmitted.
quote: Final approval of plans is valid for twelve (12) months. Construction must begin within this period. If not, plans must be re-submitted and reviewed again.
source_label: Ashton Estates, Architectural Standards and Review Procedures for Residential Construction (posted on ashtonestates.net; Sec. 14 amended October 21, 2004), Sec. 7

fact: The Ashton Estates declaration lets the committee set a review fee in its guidelines, even one based on a project's estimated cost; the posted standards and application name no fee.
quote: The Association Architectural Review Committee may, in its guidelines or rules, provide for the payment of a fee to accompany each request for approval of any proposed Improvement to Property. … such as based upon the estimated cost of the proposed Improvement to Property.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article IX, Section 9
notes: No fee appears in the Architectural Standards, the ARC Application PDF or the ARC Application page (read 2026-09-26).

fact: The Ashton Estates declaration requires an applicant to get every permit and approval a governmental authority requires, including City of Greeley building approvals, before construction starts.
quote: Applicant shall obtain, prior to commencement of construction of any Improvements to Property, all permits, licenses, certificates, consents and any other approvals necessary or required pursuant to any law, ordinance, resolution, order, rule or regulation of any governmental authority having jurisdiction … The Governmental Approvals shall be deemed to include, but not be limited to, building approvals by the City of Greeley, Colorado.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for Ashton Estates and the Ashton Estates Community Association, recorded in Weld County February 21, 1995, reception 2427196, Article IX, Section 13

fact: Ashton Estates' bylaws make its Architectural Review Committee three people appointed by the Executive Board for staggered three-year terms.
quote: If activated by the Executive Board of the Association the members of the Committee shall include three persons appointed by the Executive Board and shall serve staggered three (3) year terms as determined by the Board.
source_label: Bylaws of the Ashton Estates Community Association, Article VII, Section 1
notes: The association's home page lists three ARC members (names and e-mail addresses not reproduced here).

notes: Owner and board member names elided.

fact: At Ashton Estates' 2023 annual meeting an owner explained that buyers had been told the lots would have non-potable irrigation water, that the developer sold the water rights to the City of Greeley, and that the partly installed thin-walled Schedule 50 PVC lines tested by the city are not sufficient for high-pressure irrigation.
quote: … when the community was under development purchasers were told that the properties would have non-potable water for irrigation. At the same time the developer had also sold the water rights to the City of Greeley. As part of the development thin-walled PVC pipeline was partially installed on the majority of the lots. The PVC was scheduled 50, which can only have limited pressure and would be sturdy enough only for drip irrigation. The city has located and tested the pipes and they are not sufficient for high pressure irrigation. … the city has stated that the community would be responsible for maintaining the pipes and repairing any new or existing damage. Therefore it has been suggested that the cost of this development is greater than the possible savings that homeowners would receive from the 30 percent decrease in water bills.
source_label: Ashton Estates Community Association 2023 Annual Meeting minutes, September 28, 2023 (in the 2024 Annual Meeting Packet)
notes: Speaker's name elided. The account is an owner's report to the meeting, not a city statement.

fact: Ashton Estates' association still lists a Non-Potable Water Committee on its website.
quote: Committees Non-Potable Water Committee
source_label: Ashton Estates Homeowners Association website, home page (Board and Committees)
notes: Member names not reproduced. No posted document after the 2023 minutes reports on the project.

fact: Ashton Estates' neighborhood standards name City of Greeley water as the neighborhood's water utility.

fact: Greeley builds each single-family water budget from household size, the irrigable square footage of the yard and real-time weather, so a yard half the size of a neighbor's gets half the outdoor budget, and it asks customers to report a changed irrigated area.
quote: A water budget consists of: Family size (number of people who live in the home) Landscape around the home (irrigable square footage of yard) Real-time weather conditions … But if your yard is half the size of your neighbor's, your outdoor water budget will be half the amount of your neighbor's. … How do I adjust my persons per household or irrigated area? Please let us know if anything needs to be corrected or has recently changed!
source_label: City of Greeley Water & Sewer, Budget Your Water (and its FAQ)
notes: A town-wide fact kept here because this page leans on it for two-acre lots; it can move to local/greeley-co.json when that file is next edited. The page does not say how artificial turf is counted in irrigable area.
